policy: research authoring index only; not runtime admission

waves.focus: 2025 systematic review/meta-analysis of eight human musculoskeletal-pain studies; possible analgesic effect with substantial heterogeneity and no proof of equivalence to standard analgesics.
2026 PCOS review combining four human and four animal studies; human pooled lipids and testosterone were null, so clinical-feature signals must not be conflated with hormonal/lipid efficacy.
2024 review of 29 RCTs/1,879 participants; low-certainty nasal-symptom signals and no clear difference from antihistamines in limited comparisons; category-level only.
2024 nine-RCT/558-participant stress-anxiety meta-analysis; PSS/Hamilton-anxiety/cortisol signals with mild-moderate adverse events and uncertain long-term safety.
2025 23-RCT skin-aging meta-analysis; overall hydration/elasticity/wrinkle signals disappeared in non-industry-funded/high-quality subgroups, making funding and study quality first-class modifiers.
2024 six-RCT/339-participant obesity meta-analysis; body weight, BMI and waist outcomes were null overall, providing a direct counterweight to weight-loss claims.
2025 49-study GRADE meta-analysis of cardiovascular/metabolic risk factors; multiple pooled surrogate signals with broad heterogeneity and no clinical-event inference.
2025 RCT meta-analysis of insulin resistance/sensitivity; overall evidence did not establish meaningful HOMA-IR/fasting-insulin benefit across pomegranate products.
2025 38-RCT synthesis; oxidative-stress markers improved while CRP, IL-6 and TNF-alpha were null, separating antioxidant biomarker effects from broad anti-inflammatory claims.
2025 dose-response meta-analysis of 53 RCTs/2,306 participants; cardiometabolic risk-factor evidence remains endpoint- and preparation-specific.
2025 GRADE dose-response meta-analysis of adult blood-pressure RCTs; blood-pressure effects require dose/duration/baseline-status context and should not imply cardiovascular-event prevention.

2026 umbrella review of 16 systematic reviews/113 RCTs/7,983 participants; skin and musculoskeletal signals were more consistent than oral/cardiometabolic outcomes; category-level heterogeneity retained.
2024 16-RCT/492-participant cognition meta-analysis; memory/attention/processing-speed signals with global cognition and executive-function nulls and low-to-moderate certainty.
2025 systematic review/meta-analysis of 24 exercise studies; circulating CoQ10 increased but exercise-performance effects were limited/inconsistent—useful counterweight to ergogenic marketing.
2025 seven-small-trial mood meta-analysis; some depression-scale signals, BDI and anxiety nulls, with small samples and clinical-population heterogeneity.
2025 RCT meta-analysis of probiotics/prebiotics/synbiotics for anxiety, depression and sleep; intervention class and strain/product identity remain distinct.
2026 60-study/6,329-participant IBS review; peppermint-oil and Chinese-herbal signals coexist with limited-quality evidence and insufficient data for several plants.
2025 T2D-specific systematic review/meta-analysis of CoQ10 effects on lipids and blood pressure; disease-population and endpoint boundaries retained.
2024 24-RCT/9,660-participant dose-response cognition meta-analysis in adults >=40 without dementia; domain/time/dose trends should not become a universal cognitive-enhancement claim.
2025 systematic review/meta-analysis of placebo-controlled RCTs in healthy adults; cognitive effects remain domain-specific and the authors characterize evidence as promising but not conclusive.
2024 systematic review of 12 RCTs/703 adults; cardiometabolic effects remain short-duration and pure-OLE specific.
Seven-RCT/472-participant BP meta-analysis; modest SBP/DBP reductions with nonlinear dose/duration signals and subgroup dependence.

2025 12-week DB-RCT in 202 adults with subclinical depressive symptoms; modest depression benefit, most secondary outcomes null, sleep benefit only exploratory in a more-impaired subgroup; proprietary Affron identity retained.

2024 meta-analysis comparing saffron with SSRIs; depression/anxiety differences were nonsignificant while adverse events were fewer with saffron; direct-comparator evidence does not establish broad interchangeability.
Sleep meta-analysis across heterogeneous populations; PSQI/ISI/RSQ signals with limited long-term safety evidence and no generic dose recommendation.

2025 network meta-analysis of probiotic strains/combinations in adults with T2D; glycemic effects are strain/product and disease-population specific, and ranking does not equal head-to-head superiority.
2025 network meta-analysis of turmeric preparations for knee OA; product/formulation identity and network-comparison limitations retained.
2025 CKD-specific RCT meta-analysis of inflammatory, lipid, hematologic and anthropometric markers; disease-population surrogate evidence only.
2026 umbrella review of 45 systematic reviews/129 associations; broad multi-outcome evidence with GRADE credibility differences across endpoints.
2025 knee-OA systematic review/meta-analysis; pain/function findings remain short-term, indication-specific and preparation-sensitive.
2024 umbrella meta-analysis of prior OA meta-analyses; useful for consistency/heterogeneity assessment but not a substitute for formulation-specific RCT evidence.
2025 systematic review of 30 trials in T2D/prediabetes/metabolic syndrome; modest glycemic signals plus mechanistic microbiome readouts, with intervention classes kept separate.
2025 knee-OA RCT meta-analysis of serum inflammatory biomarkers; biomarker findings remain distinct from patient-reported pain/function efficacy.
2025 16-RCT T2D meta-analysis; FBG/HbA1c/TC/LDL signals with 2-h glucose, insulin, HOMA, TG, HDL, liver/kidney, weight and BMI nulls.
2024 30-study glycemic meta-analysis; FBS/HbA1c signals with insulin and HOMA-IR nulls and extreme heterogeneity.
2026 31-trial metabolic-disease meta-analysis; modest weight/BMI/BP/glycemic changes with central-adiposity and insulin-resistance nulls.
2025/2026 ED systematic review/meta-analysis of randomized trials; erectile-function evidence remains indication-specific and separated from testosterone/bodybuilding claims.
2025 eight-RCT/372-participant meta-analysis; SBP/DBP and waist signals with weight and BMI nulls.
2024 54-RCT/3,000-participant inflammation meta-analysis; CRP/IL-6 reductions with TNF-alpha null and high heterogeneity.
2025 umbrella review of chia meta-analyses; broad health claims graded by AMSTAR-2/GRADE, preserving low-certainty and inconsistent outcomes.
2025 systematic review/meta-analysis of moderate-high-dose astaxanthin and lipid profiles; lipid endpoints remain dose/formulation dependent.
2025 meta-analysis in overweight/obese adults; intermediate-disease-marker evidence only, with heterogeneous populations and surrogate endpoints.
2025 systematic meta-analysis of RCTs on cardiovascular/metabolic markers; multi-endpoint cardiometabolic evidence with no event-level inference.
2024 updated randomized-trial meta-analysis of anthropometric indices; weight/BMI/waist effects remain preparation/population dependent.
2025 CRP dose-response meta-analysis; inflammatory biomarker evidence remains surrogate and distinct from clinical anti-inflammatory efficacy.
2024 glycemic systematic review/meta-analysis; FBG/HbA1c/insulin evidence is limited by a small heterogeneous RCT base.
2023/2024 sex-hormone meta-analysis; FSH, SHBG, testosterone, free-androgen index and DHEAS were not significantly changed—useful endocrine counterweight.
29-RCT metabolic-syndrome meta-analysis; FPG/TG/HDL/waist/SBP signals with DBP and BMI nulls.
2025 updated 26-RCT glycemic synthesis; FBG/2hPPG/HbA1c/insulin signals with HOMA-IR null and substantial heterogeneity.
Metabolic-syndrome RCT meta-analysis of lipid and glycemic indices; disease-population and endpoint specificity retained.
2024 systematic review/meta-analysis in trained young men; maximal-intensity performance evidence is sex-, training-status-, duration-, and chronic-supplementation specific.
2025 systematic review/meta-analysis for hyperemesis gravidarum; pregnancy-specific nausea/vomiting evidence across differing ginger forms and active comparators.
2024 network meta-analysis of cranberry juice/tablets and increased fluids for UTI prevention; product form and comparator identity remain explicit.
2024/2025 PAC-dose meta-analysis; prevention signal concentrated in products providing at least a specified proanthocyanidin threshold, reinforcing composition-specificity.
International-guideline-supporting PCOS systematic review/meta-analysis; some metabolic/reproductive signals but broad outcome uncertainty and generally mild GI tolerability versus metformin.
2025 systematic review of ginger meta-analyses; umbrella-level synthesis across inflammation, T2D, oxidative stress and pregnancy nausea with indication-specific evidence kept separate.
2024 25-RCT/1,024-participant metabolic-syndrome meta-analysis; BP/FBG/TG signals with HDL null and no universal dose inference.
2026 dose-response meta-analysis of aerobic time-trial RCTs; low and moderate acute doses improved completion time, with no qualifying high-dose evidence and no dosing recommendation.
2024 CYP1A2 genotype/exercise meta-analysis; genotype appeared to modify ergogenic response, with strong caution about small CC-genotype samples.
2025 resistance-exercise meta-analysis; acute caffeine improved mean velocity/power with subgroup differences by sex and habitual use.
2025 17-RCT/971-participant GRADE review; selected BMI/creatinine/GPx/heart-rate signals but most cardiometabolic endpoints null and overall certainty very low.
2025 systematic review of lion's mane human/preclinical evidence; limited RCT cognition signals with substantial evidence-type heterogeneity.
2024 cycling-sprint meta-analysis; dietary nitrate improved time-to-peak power but not mean, peak, or minimum power—performance-domain specificity preserved.
2025 systematic review of seven interventional sleep studies; sleep evidence remains small and heterogeneous across tart-cherry products/outcomes.
Systematic review/meta-analysis of cardiopulmonary responses during maximal graded exercise; physiologic responses are exercise-test specific and distinct from performance outcomes.
2024 systematic review of expectancy/placebo effects in sport and exercise; useful context separating pharmacologic caffeine effects from expectancy effects.
2025 40-RCT review of oral supplements for photoaging; collagen/flavanol/polyphenol signals coexist with null hyaluronic-acid/lycopene/carotenoid outcomes.
2025 pharmacovigilance scoping analysis of herbal adverse-reaction signals; safety surveillance evidence only, not incidence or causal-risk estimates.
2026 systematic review of 30 RCTs/19 oral herbal interventions; high heterogeneity, with black cohosh/dong quai trials among null results.
2025 21-RCT/1,981-participant menopausal-syndrome meta-analysis; multi-herb formula and adjunctive-treatment contexts remain product specific.
2025 60-study/6,127-participant meta-analysis; modest lipid signals across heterogeneous plant-derived supplements, with soy/phytoestrogen subgroup concentration.
2026 network meta-analysis of herbal products on metabolic outcomes in MASLD; rankings remain network-level and formulation-specific.
2026 FDA CAERS disproportionality analysis; herbal/botanical and weight-loss categories carried safety signals, but spontaneous-reporting data cannot establish incidence or causality.
Updated meta-analysis of plant-derived supplements for menopausal symptoms; pooled symptom improvements coexist with heterogeneous products and generally suboptimal evidence quality.
2024 RCT meta-analysis of probiotics/prebiotics/synbiotics/FMT and related gut-microbiota interventions in MASLD; intervention classes, duration and mechanistic endpoints remain separate.

Systematic review/meta-analysis of long-chain omega-3 for anxiety/depression in adults; depression signals were stronger in EPA-enriched interventions while anxiety evidence was sparse and heterogeneity/publication-bias concerns remain.

Large dose-response depression meta-analysis; symptom reduction was concentrated in people with existing depression, while prevention of incident depression in general populations was not established.
15-RCT/415-participant review in middle-aged/older adults; blood-pressure effects combine isolated L-citrulline and watermelon interventions, so compound-versus-food-matrix identity is preserved.
Six-RCT/162-participant meta-analysis in cold exposure; blood-pressure findings are environmental-context specific and not a general resting-BP claim.
Seven-RCT/325-participant meta-analysis in depressive disorders; mood evidence is diagnosis-specific and limited by small trials/formulation differences.
RCT meta-analysis of adiponectin/leptin; overall effects were limited/null with selected NAFLD or longer-duration subgroup signals, making subgroup dependence explicit.
Systematic review of randomized human trials examining lycopene intake and mental-health outcomes; evidence remains heterogeneous and outcome-specific.
Systematic review/meta-analysis in non-anemic iron-deficient adults; subjective fatigue improved while objective physical-capacity outcomes did not, preserving symptom-versus-performance distinction.

Recent depression meta-analysis; depressive-symptom signal did not translate consistently into response/remission or adverse-event superiority, and any proposed EPA/dose pattern remains evidence metadata rather than a dosing recommendation.
Systematic review of magnesium for self-reported anxiety and sleep; most included studies reported some benefit, but samples, formulations and outcome methods were small/heterogeneous.
Blood-pressure meta-analysis; overall systolic/diastolic effects were null, with an obesity-related DBP subgroup signal that should not be generalized.
2026 meta-analysis of ambulatory blood pressure from five RCTs/202 participants; ambulatory-BP evidence remains small and protocol-specific.

Systematic review of 120 randomized prevention trials involving roughly 1.67 million participants; clinically important outcomes and safety vary strongly by population, baseline status and prevention context.
48-RCT/3,255-participant meta-analysis of inflammatory and oxidative-stress biomarkers; biomarker effects are surrogate evidence and do not establish disease modification.
Dose-response meta-analysis in type 2 diabetes; glycemic/cardiometabolic findings remain T2D- and endpoint-specific.
Cardiac-surgery meta-analysis of postoperative outcomes; perioperative evidence cannot be inherited by routine outpatient supplementation.
41-RCT/~2,900-participant glycemic meta-analysis with high heterogeneity; pooled biomarker changes require population/formulation boundaries.
Randomized-trial blood-pressure meta-analysis; modest pooled effects are heterogeneous and should remain distinct from ambulatory-BP evidence.
Metabolic-syndrome related meta-analysis; cardiometabolic biomarker evidence remains surrogate and phenotype-specific.
Systematic review/meta-analysis of omega-3 for prevention/treatment of depression; prevention and treatment strata remain separate.
Large randomized-trial synthesis found little or no preventive effect on depression/anxiety in people without baseline disorders—important counterweight to broad mental-health claims.
Updated randomized-trial synthesis in steatotic liver disease; hepatic/metabolic outcomes stay disease-specific and separate from generic vitamin-D efficacy.
2024 systematic review of eight human trials on sleep; most adult studies suggested better sleep quality, while sleep-disorder and nonadult findings were inconsistent and more trials are needed.

2024 GRADE meta-analysis of 35 Hashimoto-thyroiditis studies; TSH/TPOAb/MDA signals with several thyroid hormones, TGAb, thyroid volume and immune markers null; autoimmune-thyroid population boundary retained.
2026 umbrella review of six meta-analyses/17 RCTs; modest systolic-BP signal, overall DBP null with diabetes subgroup signal, and low certainty of evidence.
2025 MASLD meta-analysis of 12 RCTs/657 participants; liver-enzyme and selected metabolic/inflammatory signals remain disease-, strain-, and outcome-specific.

27-study/1,691-participant MASLD comparison of curcumin, resveratrol and silymarin; intervention-specific steatosis/transaminase/metabolic effects must not be collapsed into a generic polyphenol claim.
2025 systematic review of 17 human oral-health studies spanning multiple herbal extracts; adjunctive gingivitis/periodontitis evidence is product- and route-specific.
15-RCT/905-participant NAFLD GRADE review; ALT/AST decreased with curcumin while ALP was null and curcumin-plus-piperine aminotransferase effects were nonsignificant.

26-RCT/1,266-participant periodontal comparison with chlorhexidine; plaque/gingival/bleeding outcomes similar while chlorhexidine was superior for probing depth/attachment loss overall; very high heterogeneity/risk of bias retained.
21-study CKD meta-analysis; modest BUN/CRP signals with heterogeneous renal, uremic-toxin and metabolic outcomes; CKD-specific and strain/intervention-class dependent.
2024 NAFLD systematic review/meta-analysis of glycemic, lipid, BP, inflammatory and anthropometric outcomes; multi-endpoint evidence remains disease-specific and heterogeneous.

15-study/835-participant NAFLD meta-regression; AST improved while ALT was null overall, high heterogeneity persisted, and adding piperine did not improve aminotransferases—important counterweight to other syntheses.
Network meta-analysis comparing seven natural products in NAFLD; indirect rankings and product heterogeneity prevent ingredient-wide superiority claims.
2024 network meta-analysis of probiotic combinations in NAFLD; strain/composition rankings are indirect and cannot be generalized across probiotics.
2026 11-RCT/726-participant diabetic-kidney-disease meta-analysis; creatinine/eGFR and related signals remain DKD-, strain-, and duration-specific.
15-RCT/899-participant NAFLD meta-analysis; ALT/HOMA-IR/insulin improved while fasting glucose, HbA1c, AST, lipids, IL-6 and TNF-alpha were null.
2026 Bayesian network meta-analysis of dietary supplements and pharmacologic agents in MAFLD; ranking evidence is indirect and outcome-specific.
2026 review of 90 periodontal RCTs/33 pooled trials across curcumin, resveratrol, propolis, Aloe, green-tea catechins, omega-3 and others; adjunct/route/product boundaries retained.
Umbrella review of randomized evidence in IBS; most nutritional interventions had small low/very-low-certainty effects, with stronger evidence concentrated in probiotics and low-FODMAP diets.
Nine-study/615-participant NAFLD meta-analysis of probiotics plus exercise versus exercise alone; selected liver/lipid/HOMA-IR signals with HDL/insulin/FBG nulls; combination-only.
Systematic review of vitamin-D therapy in adults with CKD assessing mortality, cardiovascular, bone and kidney outcomes; CKD-MBD context and clinically important outcomes retained.
2025 78-study PCOS nutraceutical review; fasting-insulin/LH/SHBG signals with inconsistent follicle-count/menstrual outcomes and substantial intervention heterogeneity.
2025 oral-mucositis meta-analysis of randomized trials in cancer therapy; Aloe evidence is cancer-treatment-context and route/formulation specific.
2025 network meta-analysis of 79 RCTs/5,501 women with PCOS; supplement rankings are endpoint-specific indirect evidence, not head-to-head proof.
2024 five-study/286-participant psoriasis meta-analysis; PASI/DLQI signals come from a small disease-specific probiotic evidence base.
2025 systematic review of clinical phytotherapy in PCOS; herb/product-specific findings must remain separated from category-level efficacy.
2025 umbrella meta-analysis of dietary supplements in PCOS; pathway-level metabolic/hormonal signals across inositol, probiotics, omega-3, curcumin and others remain intervention-specific.
2025 21-RCT/1,463-participant plaque-psoriasis network meta-analysis; no supplement dominated all outcomes and certainty was low-to-moderate.
2025 systematic review/dose-response meta-analysis of fertility outcomes in PCOS; reproductive evidence remains PCOS-specific and distinct from generic carnitine metabolic claims.
2025 seven-RCT/263-participant systematic review of combined creatine+beta-alanine; high-intensity performance signals are combination-specific and evidence is predominantly male.
2026 52-RCT network meta-analysis; creatine alone had the most consistent high-intensity performance effects while beta-alanine was task-specific and combined supplementation showed no added synergy.
Six-study/95-participant meta-analysis found caffeine+nitrate co-supplementation did not outperform caffeine or nitrate alone for time trials, heart rate or oxygen uptake.
2025 network meta-analysis of 30 RCTs/693 athletes comparing protein, creatine, beta-alanine, HMB, vitamin D and nitrate across energy-system outcomes; indirect rankings remain outcome-specific.

2025 umbrella review of 20 meta-analyses/180 primary studies/2,672 participants; benefits were domain-specific, several performance outcomes were null, and most underlying reviews were low/critically-low quality.
2025 meta-analysis of 34 RCTs/2,390 adults on cognitive outcomes and adverse events; cognition evidence remains strain-, population-, test-, and duration-specific.
2025 network meta-analysis of 35 RCTs/991 athletes; supplement effects on strength, sprint, jump and muscle mass differed by outcome, with most trials having some risk-of-bias concerns.
2025 review of 46 studies/928 elite athletes; caffeine showed more consistent sport-performance effects than nitrate, while beta-alanine and recovery supplements were sport/context dependent.
2024 systematic review of 36 cycling studies/701 participants spanning caffeine, creatine, bicarbonate, beta-alanine, nitrate and combinations; sport- and intervention-specific evidence only.
2025 systematic review/meta-analysis of 16 randomized studies testing performance-enhancing supplement combinations; combination effects must not be attributed to individual ingredients.
2025 six-study/424-patient insomnia meta-analysis; PSQI improved with moderate certainty while depression-score evidence was very-low certainty.
2025 umbrella review of probiotic meta-analyses for cognitive-related outcomes; strength/quality of evidence varies substantially by population and endpoint.
2026 13-study/890-participant adult sleep meta-analysis; modest PSQI/ISI signals with strain/product and baseline-sleep heterogeneity.
24-RCT/7,557-participant cognition meta-analysis; small global-cognition effect, no consistent specific-domain effect, with stronger signals in vulnerable/deficient subgroups.
2025 20-study/1,093-participant meta-analysis of creatine plus exercise in older adults; strength/fat-percentage signals with total-body BMD null; combination/context specific.
2024 systematic review found brain creatine increases but cognitive effects remain equivocal, providing a counterweight to positive cognition meta-analyses.
Systematic review of 20 adult RCTs found mixed cognition results and did not support a consistent cognitive-enhancement effect—important counterweight to later positive syntheses.
RCT meta-analysis of fatigue; fatigue-reduction signal stronger for CoQ10-only formulations than compound products, with formulation and symptom-context boundaries.
2024 18-RCT/1,147-participant review of protein+resistance training and gait speed in older adults; exercise-combination and aging-population context retained.
2025 older-adult meta-analysis of whey protein with/without resistance training; body-composition, strength and cardiometabolic outcomes remain context- and co-intervention-specific.
Systematic review/meta-analysis found negligible benefit of a single oral dose for continuous running performance, providing a sport-task-specific null.
2024 18-study meta-analysis; BCAA reduced selected CK and muscle-soreness timepoints after exercise-induced damage but did not improve LDH; recovery biomarker/symptom evidence only.
2025 swimming meta-analysis; bicarbonate raised blood bicarbonate/lactate/pH but did not significantly improve 200-m time—physiology-performance dissociation retained.
2024 overview of 11 systematic reviews; CK/muscle-soreness recovery signals with no effect on muscle-performance recovery and notable review-quality limitations.

2026 13-RCT/561-participant meta-analysis in adults >=50 found no meaningful added benefit of HMB+resistance training for fat mass, muscle mass or strength; strong counterweight to routine-adjunct claims.
2024 systematic review of chromium in T2D; possible glycemic/lipid signals coexist with wide formulation/dose/duration heterogeneity and uncertain long-term risk.
2025 overweight/obesity meta-analysis; selected insulin-resistance/metabolic effects with several near-null estimates and mixed anthropometric/BP/liver findings.
2025 dose-response meta-analysis of 10 RCTs; BP reduction was much larger in hypertensive than normotensive participants, emphasizing baseline-BP dependence.
Systematic review/meta-analysis of vitamin-K supplementation and cardiovascular risk factors; biomarker/risk-factor evidence is not clinical-event prevention evidence.
Updated randomized-trial meta-analysis of inflammatory mediators; inflammatory biomarker evidence remains surrogate and population dependent.
2026 randomized-trial meta-analysis in metabolic diseases; cardiometabolic, inflammatory and oxidative-stress findings remain phenotype- and endpoint-specific.
2025 dose-response meta-analysis of 27 experimental human studies on blood lipids; possible nonlinear lipid effects and overexposure concerns remain first-class.
75-study GRADE meta-analysis; several glycemic/lipid/inflammatory/oxidative markers improved while LDL, HDL, insulin, BP and liver enzymes were null.
2026 13-study/14,539-participant CHD meta-analysis of folic acid+B6+B12; homocysteine lowering and vascular outcomes remain distinct from hard-event efficacy.
21-RCT/1,625-participant meta-analysis; isolated B12 lowered homocysteine, a surrogate biomarker, without implying cardiovascular-event reduction.
2026 36-RCT hyperhomocysteinemia meta-analysis; tHcy and modest BP/lipid surrogate changes with high heterogeneity/bias and no adjudicated hard cardiovascular endpoints.
Randomized-trial meta-analysis found little overall lipid benefit, increased SBP, and selected LDL/TC subgroup effects—important cardiovascular-safety counterweight.
Ten-RCT/526-participant cardiometabolic-disease meta-analysis; insulin/HOMA-IR/HDL signals with FPG, TC, TG, LDL and VLDL nulls and high heterogeneity.
20-RCT GRADE dose-response review; fasting-insulin/QUICKI signals with FBS, HbA1c and HOMA-IR nulls.
Ten-RCT/509-participant T2D meta-analysis of glucose/lipid outcomes; disease-specific evidence with formulation and trial-quality limitations.
28-study T2D meta-analysis; FPG/insulin/HbA1c/HOMA-IR pooled reductions accompanied by extreme heterogeneity for several outcomes.
Older diabetes meta-analysis including mono- and combination supplementation; glycemic/lipid signals with inadequate long-term safety evidence and combination uncertainty.
22-study/41,633-participant BP meta-analysis; small SBP/DBP reductions with dose/duration/subgroup variability—large sample but surrogate outcome.
Hypertension-specific meta-analysis; BP lowering was stronger with lower baseline potassium, higher sodium and no antihypertensive therapy.
23-RCT/1,213-participant essential-hypertension meta-analysis; modest BP reduction with moderate heterogeneity and adjunctive-context framing.
Umbrella/hierarchical synthesis of nutrient supplements for T2D; most HbA1c evidence was low or very-low certainty and intervention-specific.
Observational dose-response meta-analysis found a U-shaped association between blood selenium and metabolic syndrome; association evidence must not be treated as supplementation efficacy.
Observational GRADE dose-response meta-analysis linked higher dietary calcium with lower MetS odds; dietary association is not supplement-trial evidence.
Earlier cardiometabolic RCT meta-analysis; glycemic/lipid signals with BP/anthropometric nulls, useful historical comparison with newer zinc syntheses.
Older metabolic-disease RCT meta-analysis of glucose/lipid profiles; retained as historical evidence to compare with later contradictory selenium syntheses.
2024 30-year historical assessment of clinically relevant botanical-drug interactions; mechanism and clinical-evidence strength remain interaction-specific.
Systematic review/meta-analysis of clinical herb-drug interaction studies; clinically important St John's wort, echinacea and green-tea interactions illustrate transporter/enzyme-specific risk.
Systematic review of 47 clinical pharmacokinetic interaction trials; strongest evidence centered on St John's wort, with limited inference for most botanicals.
Clinical/pharmacokinetic review highlights major gaps between in-vitro predictions and human interaction trials; preclinical enzyme effects must not be treated as proven clinical interactions.
USP comprehensive hepatotoxicity review; concentrated extract, fasting/bolus exposure and interindividual susceptibility are key context, distinct from brewed tea.
Systematic review of 34 RCTs found few mostly mild liver-enzyme adverse events and no serious hepatic events; useful RCT counterweight to case-report hepatotoxicity evidence.

Italian phytovigilance plus systematic case review linked high-bioavailability turmeric/curcumin supplements with acute hepatitis; concomitant exposures and case-report causality limitations retained.
Systematic safety review of 159 human intervention studies; hepatic risk concentrated in high-bolus catechin-rich extracts and differed from brewed tea/food exposures.
2026 USP safety review concluded clinically apparent hepatotoxicity is rare but real enough to justify cautionary labeling; idiosyncratic/genetic susceptibility and concomitant products retained.
Systematic kava safety review covering hepatotoxicity, adverse effects, interactions and preparation issues; product/extract type and causality uncertainty remain explicit.

2026 systematic review of 31 studies/32 liver-injury cases; predominantly cholestatic injury, frequent incomplete exposure data/polysubstance use, and several transplant cases; case evidence does not establish incidence.
2026 scoping review of 25 reported liver-injury patients; cholestatic/mixed patterns predominated, with case-series evidence and product/concomitant-exposure limitations.

Systematic review of prospective clinical trials found repeated reductions in systemic bioavailability of conventional drugs during St John's wort exposure; interaction evidence is extract/hyperforin dependent.
31-study CYP3A systematic review; high-hyperforin extracts consistently induced CYP3A while low-hyperforin extracts showed less/no effect, making constituent standardization central.
18-RCT/1,985-participant meta-analysis of hemostasis outcomes found no clear increased bleeding-risk signal with standardized Ginkgo extract—counterweight to bleeding case reports.
18-study meta-analysis linked chronic glycyrrhizic-acid-containing licorice exposure with increased BP and reduced potassium/renin/aldosterone; cardiovascular-risk context retained.
2025 clinical interaction/coagulation analysis found associations between Ginkgo-drug interactions, bleeding symptoms and abnormal coagulation, with medication-specific patterns.
Meta-analysis of five randomized trials of isopropanolic black-cohosh extract found no adverse liver-function effect, an important formulation-specific counterweight to spontaneous reports.
Updated systematic review of seven popular herbs documented extensive St John's wort interactions and more limited evidence for ginkgo, ginseng, garlic, echinacea, saw palmetto and kava.
Causality-focused survey of purported black-cohosh liver-injury cases found major case-quality limitations and no confirmed causality under liver-specific assessment methods.
2024 systematic review of medicinal/edible fruit adverse events; serious events were present and were often associated with excess exposure or young children; species identity preserved.
2025 analytical safety study documented lead/nickel contamination in tested adaptogenic supplements, demonstrating product-quality risk rather than intrinsic botanical pharmacology.
Systematic review/meta-analysis of 936 reported HILI cases across 79 herbs/products; causality and incidence limitations retained while high-frequency implicated products are mapped.
Pooled analysis of 428 herbal/dietary-supplement liver-injury cases; severe outcomes occurred, but case-report aggregation cannot estimate population incidence.
Systematic safety review found clinical adverse events generally rare/mild/reversible while serious spontaneous reports existed with uncertain causality; historical safety context retained.

2025 updated acute-respiratory-infection prevention meta-analysis of 40 studies/61,589 participants; overall protection did not reach statistical significance, providing a major counterweight to earlier positive syntheses.
2025 pediatric ARI meta-analysis of 17 RCTs/18,372 participants; overall infection incidence, hospitalization, recovery and mortality were null, with subgroup/safety signals kept exploratory.
2024 43-RCT/49,320-participant ARI-prevention meta-analysis; overall pooled effect was null and subgroup dose/frequency findings must not become dosing recommendations.
2025 allergic-rhinitis meta-analysis of five RCTs; overall symptom benefit was nonsignificant with extreme heterogeneity, while selected no-corticosteroid subgroup findings remain exploratory.
2026 meta-analysis spanning upper-respiratory infection, allergic rhinitis and chronic rhinosinusitis; disease, strain and product identity must remain separated.
2026 pediatric respiratory-infection network meta-analysis of eight RCTs/1,158 participants; strain-specific signals were low-certainty and network rankings are not head-to-head proof.
Seven-trial/575-participant common-cold lozenge meta-analysis; roughly one-third shorter duration in selected high-dose lozenge trials, with formulation and dose context essential.
Individual-patient-data meta-analysis of three zinc-acetate trials/199 participants; shorter cold duration with no clear modification by allergy/status variables, but restricted to acetate lozenges.
17-trial/2,121-participant common-cold meta-analysis; shorter duration in adults but not children, with more adverse events and substantial heterogeneity.
Older systematic review found evidence insufficient/inconclusive for zinc in the common cold; retained as historical counterweight.
Six-RCT/1,551-adult URTI meta-analysis; low-quality evidence suggested selected incidence/duration benefits with very high heterogeneity for episode-rate outcomes.
Systematic review of zinc dose/formulation in common-cold trials; heterogeneity in salts, lozenge composition and dosing prevents a generic zinc equivalence claim.
Individual-patient-data analysis of three zinc-acetate trials found faster recovery rates; formulation-specific and small-trial evidence.
Randomized placebo-controlled zinc-acetate lozenge trial in 87 common-cold cases found no meaningful recovery benefit, providing a direct counterweight to prior positive lozenge meta-analyses.
Historical zinc-lozenge meta-analysis with null/inconclusive findings; useful for tracing evidence evolution and formulation heterogeneity.
Meta-analysis of vitamin C for severe common-cold symptoms; treatment-context and symptom-severity findings remain distinct from prevention claims.
Respiratory-infection meta-analysis; incidence/severity were not consistently reduced while illness duration was shorter in selected analyses.
Meta-analysis of vitamin C used with antiviral therapy for common cold; combination-treatment evidence cannot be attributed to vitamin C alone.
Older randomized-trial review of probiotics for acute URTI prevention; incidence signals with less consistent duration evidence and substantial intervention heterogeneity.
Six-RCT acute-bronchitis evidence for Pelargonium sidoides preparations; acute indication and standardized-product identity retained.
Systematic review of vitamin-D supplementation for respiratory infections in children under six; findings were inconsistent and age-specific.
2021 large ARI meta-analysis; modest protective signal in some analyses with regimen/population modifiers, retained to compare with later null updates.
Older respiratory-infection meta-analysis reported a protective signal but also heterogeneity/publication-bias concerns; historical context only.
Early small-trial respiratory-infection meta-analysis suggested benefit; retained as historical evidence showing how conclusions changed as trial volume increased.
Older Cochrane-style common-cold synthesis; possible duration benefit alongside adverse events and major formulation/dose heterogeneity.

Five-RCT/400-participant sleep meta-analysis; small pooled sleep benefit with stronger subgroup signals in insomnia/longer exposure, but extract/duration heterogeneity and no generic dose recommendation.
22-RCT aromatherapy meta-analysis; anxiety and selected physiologic stress signals, with route-specific evidence and substantial contextual heterogeneity.
Nine-trial cognition meta-analysis; attention-processing-speed signals with standardized-extract and chronic-use boundaries, not proof of broad nootropic enhancement.
2025/2026 review of 11 RCTs/628 adults; lavender essential oil improved pooled sleep-quality scores, but route, blinding and subjective-outcome limits remain.
Systematic review of randomized trials for menopausal vasomotor symptoms; inconsistent results and study-quality variation prevent a uniform hot-flash claim.
Updated 22-study/2,310-participant meta-analysis; overall menopausal/hot-flash signals with anxiety/depression nulls and combination-regimen heterogeneity.
11-RCT menopause meta-analysis; estradiol/Kupperman signals with hot-flash/FSH/LH nulls and extreme heterogeneity.
Older placebo-controlled meta-analysis suggesting vasomotor improvement but with significant heterogeneity; retained as historical positive evidence.
2025 six-RCT menopause systematic review/meta-analysis; menopausal-symptom evidence remains limited and indication/formulation specific.
GRADE-assessed hot-flash systematic review/meta-analysis; red-clover isoflavone efficacy remains formulation/population specific.
Cochrane review of 16 RCTs/2,027 women; no significant difference versus placebo for hot-flush frequency or menopausal symptom scores, a major counterweight to positive syntheses.
Older systematic review of six double-blind RCTs; efficacy inconsistent and uncertain, supporting explicit historical disagreement.
Eight-trial meta-analysis; modest reduction in daily hot-flash frequency with substantial heterogeneity and formulation/dose dependence.
Review/meta-analysis of isopropanolic Cimicifuga racemosa extract; product-specific menopausal evidence with manufacturer-affiliation provenance retained.
2019 CINV systematic review/meta-analysis; selected acute-vomiting/fatigue signals but many nausea/delayed outcomes null, adjunctive oncology context only.
2022 review of 23 CINV RCTs; overall acute/delayed nausea/vomiting largely null, with a limited low-dose/longer-duration acute-vomiting subgroup signal.
Ten-RCT CINV meta-analysis; historical pooled antiemetic evidence retained alongside newer conflicting syntheses.
14-study postoperative-nausea/vomiting meta-analysis; selected nausea/rescue-antiemetic outcomes improved while vomiting comparisons were mixed.
RCT meta-analysis in menopausal women; spine BMD signal with intervention-duration, geography, dose and preparation heterogeneity.
Four-RCT menopause systematic review; limited favorable symptom evidence with small samples, methodological limitations and insufficient safety evidence.
18-RCT meta-analysis; modest BMD preservation at lumbar spine/femoral neck/hip with preparation, duration and population modifiers.
Bone-turnover-marker meta-analysis in postmenopausal women; osteocalcin/BAP/PYD/DPD pooled changes were not statistically significant.
2024 umbrella review of ten RCT meta-analyses; BMD signals across several bone sites, but inherits heterogeneity and quality limits of underlying reviews.
Meta-analysis in Western peri/postmenopausal women; isoflavone mixtures did not significantly preserve lumbar-spine BMD, useful counterweight to broader positive syntheses.
63-RCT postmenopausal BMD meta-analysis; pooled bone-density signals with major intervention, duration and population heterogeneity.
2026 IBS umbrella review of 27 systematic reviews; modest symptom signals but predominantly low/very-low certainty, high review overlap, and generally weak methodology.
2025 umbrella meta-analysis across gastrointestinal disorders; diarrhea/nausea/epigastric-pain/bloating signals remain disorder-, strain-, duration-, and formulation-specific.
2025 evidence review of chronic-constipation diet/supplement strategies; psyllium, specific probiotics, magnesium oxide and selected foods show differing evidence strength, not category equivalence.
Systematic review/meta-analysis of food/vitamin/mineral supplements for chronic constipation; magnesium oxide improved several outcomes while senna/kiwifruit evidence was limited by few trials.
2025 network meta-analysis comparing probiotics, dietary management and combinations in IBS; indirect rankings and heterogeneous interventions remain research-only.
49-RCT/6,987-participant meta-analysis of herbal therapies for functional dyspepsia; broad category evidence requires product-level separation.
Cochrane review of non-Chinese herbal medicines for functional dyspepsia; individual botanicals showed mixed benefits/nulls and adverse-event differences, preventing a generic herbal claim.

13-RCT/930-participant ulcerative-colitis meta-analysis; active-disease remission signal did not reach significance, maintenance/response/mucosal healing were null, while relapse prevention in remission showed benefit.
Systematic review/meta-analysis of dietary, nutraceutical and probiotic GERD interventions; evidence was sparse and highly heterogeneous, with only selected interventions showing signals.
Updated placebo-controlled RCT meta-analysis of curcumin adjunctive therapy in IBD; UC response/remission signals with heterogeneity, but Crohn disease outcomes were not superior to placebo.
Ten-RCT/757-participant IBS-C meta-analysis; stool consistency and fecal bacterial counts improved, while abdominal pain, bloating, quality of life and adverse events were null.
Large 82-RCT/10,332-participant IBS meta-analysis; effects differed materially by strain and outcome, with certainty ranging from moderate to very low.
2024 20-study/3,011-participant IBS meta-analysis; global symptom and quality-of-life signals remain limited by heterogeneous probiotic formulations.
2024 network meta-analysis of adjunctive probiotic/prebiotic/synbiotic formulations in mild-moderate UC; formulation rankings are indirect and disease-specific.
81-RCT/9,253-participant IBS network meta-analysis; apparent strain/mixture rankings are outcome-specific and not direct head-to-head proof.
12-study/867-participant functional-dyspepsia meta-analysis; traditional multi-herb formula evidence remains formula- and comparator-specific.
2024 IBD overview plus updated RCT meta-analysis; benefit appeared more consistent in UC/pouchitis than Crohn disease, with low overall certainty.
2026 24-RCT/1,491-participant UC network meta-analysis across 14 dietary supplements; efficacy rankings remain indirect, outcome-specific and limited by trial number/quality.
2025 13-placebo-controlled-RCT IBD meta-analysis; adjunctive curcumin improved selected UC outcomes but not Crohn clinical/endoscopic remission.
33-study/2,713-participant IBD systematic review; probiotic benefit was more consistent for UC than Crohn disease, with formulation-specific differences.
2024 network meta-analysis of prebiotics/probiotics/synbiotics/FMT as IBD adjuncts; intervention-class and disease-type distinctions remain explicit.
2025 umbrella meta-analysis of IBD relapse/recurrence/remission; relapse signal versus placebo but not mesalazine, and no consistent remission benefit.
2026 review positioning plant-derived IBS treatments against guideline evidence; peppermint oil has the most consistent botanical support while many other extracts are mixed/null.
2024 systematic review of probiotic effects on quality of life across GI diseases; disease, strain, and QoL instrument heterogeneity prevent a general probiotic QoL claim.
2026 narrative evidence synthesis of diet/nutraceutical approaches in functional dyspepsia; peppermint-caraway, ginger, STW-5, curcumin and selected probiotics remain product/phenotype specific.
